importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — a telecom BTS enclosure, a labour camp block, a guard cabin, and a disaster relief unit are all 'prefabricated shelters' but look entirely different. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Wall panel material, insulation thickness, frame material, and size are non-negotiable shortlisting gates — a telecom buyer needs PUF panels with IP54 compliance; a defence buyer needs IS:1893 seismic zone compliance; a contractor needs specific floor area and flooring type. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard portable cabins and guard rooms are often quoted per unit/per piece; custom industrial and telecom shelters are quoted per sq ft. Both units appear in the market — unit must be shown to prevent price comparison errors.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per unit is a genuine market ambiguity — a buyer comparing a per-sq-ft quote against a per-unit quote cannot assess value without knowing the unit. Price cannot be interpreted or compared without unit clarity.

Price varies enormously with wall panel material, insulation grade, size, and fitout — buyers discover and compare across spec tiers, not within a fixed tier. Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive but listed price is a budget entry point; final price is always negotiated after spec equivalence is confirmed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Market is fragmented across regional fabricators with no dominant brand carrying buyer recall — buyers search by application, material, and spec, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer vs trader distinction matters for installation capability, warranty, and after-sales service — particularly for defence, railway, and telecom buyers who require site erection and commissioning. Company credentials are evaluated after spec shortlisting, not before.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental material class of the shelter — FRP, PUF, GI Sheet, and EPS panels are non-interchangeable across applications (telecom requires PUF for insulation, defence requires IS:8183-compliant panels), and drive the largest price delta across the product range.

Defines the thermal and acoustic performance grade within a panel type — non-interchangeable for application compliance (40mm for standard site offices vs 80mm for telecom/defence enclosures), with significant price delta between thickness tiers.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Telecom BTS and equipment enclosure buyers specify IP54 or higher as a mandatory compliance requirement — sellers without this spec cannot confirm eligibility for the buyer's deployment environment.
Defence, railway, and government PSU buyers specify IS:875 wind load and IS:1893 seismic zone compliance in tenders — absence of this spec prevents institutional buyers from shortlisting a listing.

Single-storey and double/multi-storey prefabricated shelters are fundamentally different products with non-overlapping price ranges and structural requirements — buyers cannot shortlist without knowing whether a seller supplies multi-storey configurations.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to the correct seller type — a telecom shelter manufacturer, a dome shelter fabricator, and a portable shelter supplier are distinct businesses; sellers need this to determine whether they can supply the required product type.
Defines the scale of the requirement — sellers need floor area to determine manufacturing feasibility, logistics, and provide an accurate price indication per sq ft.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a security cabin, site office, labour camp, or telecom BTS enclosure to determine product type, applicable compliance standards, and fitout scope — this is the primary routing signal within the Prefabricated Shelters MCAT.

Sellers manufacture in specific panel materials (PUF, FRP, MS/GI Sheet) — buyers who specify their required material allow sellers to immediately confirm supply capability and provide accurate pricing.
